# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md),
> expanding the RFC’s phase sequence into **three levels of tasks that can be committed and verified
> independently**.
>
> RFC-039’s main text is the sole authority for phase ordering and acceptance gates; this document
> is responsible only for breaking the work down to an executable granularity and recording
> conflicts that have not yet been adjudicated.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with RFC-039’s phase sequence                                        |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each of which can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 263         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                           |

**Numbering gaps (not reused)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP route
was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unassigned (2026-11-25). None of the three has
had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the entire history of this document has zero
matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can be used to verify this),
and the repository contains no references to them. `8.1` corresponds precisely to stage 1 of `05`
(test revival and completion): that stage was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8’s
numbering is aligned with its stage numbers (stage 0 → `8.0`, stage 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale
for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: every newly registered Level-2/Level-3 row
**must contain two fields**—**“Owning phase”** (the P phase to which it truly belongs, which may
differ from its current section) and **“Blocks mainline”**. `Pending scheduling` is no longer the
default status; an unspecified value means **not schedulable**. IDs must be **unique across the
entire document**; tasks on other tracks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy an `N.x` number.

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: a checked row contains only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number, if any—in one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not record the
fix, the criteria chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**:
those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a kanban board, not a
process chronicle. **Do not record adjudication labels or restate conclusions**: “User adjudication
A/B/C,” “Option A,” “Case A,” “The final implementation is…” and similar wording do not belong
here—the board answers only “complete or not”; consult the commit message and RFC-039’s decision
register for adjudications and results.

**Short hashes are determined after push**: a closure row records the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push has completed. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closure row**; see “Commit hash is obtained after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md). The closure commit itself carries no
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**Count columns contain only numbers**: the Level-1/Level-2/Level-3 counts under “Positioning and
Scope” contain only the current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong
in the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “Implementation Points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Resolution                                                                                                                                           |
| --- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 had no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how to perform the split; `annotations.rs` appears once in the directory tree in `01-routing.md`, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                            | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                               |
| G2  | **The three `include!` conversions had three owners and no implementation**. RFC-039 lists them under P4; `02` assigns their reference to itself; and §S7 of `06` also lists them. However, the change list in `02` (6 additions + 20 modifications) **does not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                         | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here          |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts plus one `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks; and `04` previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, **there are at least nine new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` has dual ownership under P4 and P9 | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table               |
| G4  | **Conflict over the fate of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                 | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision record C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                                |
| G5  | **Conflicting wording for the L2 objective**: RFC-039 and the directory index formerly described a “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | It has been converged on a **declarative precedence table + an ambiguity-free language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent / do not fill endlessly / do not
patch what should be refactored) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established
before work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, work will already be adding `mod` declarations
to `tests/mod.rs`—which is precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Approach)

Source: the vulnerability-fix half of §Implementation Points S3 in [02](02-stage-contract.md) +
**Silent-Discard-Point Audit of 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, or silently
> returning the wrong answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactoring**, but all four
> requirements must be met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and must actually
> be red); ② do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not turn into failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be removed or altered); ③ register in the same commit (this row
> identifies the error type + that phase’s revision note + a required “Error type” line in the PR
> block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible
> semantics / E external-contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still be adjudicated
> first. See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the
> expanded criteria and A–F allowlist; do not adopt “default super-refactoring + post-hoc
> registration”** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be
> distinguished from regressions, and this conflicts with both “no C5′” and “no relaxation
> whatsoever”).

**Acceptance**: vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn
them red again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 requires manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate in P9 as criteria. **Risk**:
the new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized corpus differential
baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites for
> 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (the IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, and performance
> baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects such as
> `Sorted(3)` passing silently must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3
> (converting panics to diagnostics) has no prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactoring itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by
an ordering constraint**. It is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (Rust’s
`pub(crate)` narrowing).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g’s deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite
surfaces of all four refactoring phases; reversing the order means redoing the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                      | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                    |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavioral changes must land a red criterion before code is
   changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced top-level
   bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were always exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` case from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (the new parse error + new W1001) ⇒
   update the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero differences, and any non-zero difference
   requires an explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and is not mixed with
   other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must run serially
and must not run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; whichever goes first is left to the implementer’s working context.

> **Commit correspondence (2026-10-08)**: this section’s incorporation (the P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039’s D56 were incorporated together into `97071c81b` during a
> parallel-stream cleanup of the working tree—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary
> registration + documentation of D57/D58 adjudications” and does not mention this track. History is
> not rewritten; as in the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation
> note), it is recorded in place as a post-hoc bisect anchor.

|                                                  | 4.4.4 The shared-solver observation ledger `ConsumerStats`/`CONSUMER_STATS`: every production acquisition point writes to it, while the production side has zero readers (the only read entry point is `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs`). **Decision of 2026-10-24 ① retain it**—write “the sole consumer = tests” into the doc contract (preserving the D58 observable-criteria carrier); decision ② “delete it” is not taken (that would require simultaneously rewriting 4.4.2’s acceptance criterion and recording the rationale in the 4.4 closeout “sixteen”). **Terminal state**: the three contract sentences are written into the module header and relevant item-level doc comments in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/proof/smt/backend.rs`—① the write surface = one atomic increment per acquisition through the shared entry point; ② the read surface consists **only** of `proof/smt/tests/shared.rs` (zero calls from production code); ③ `SolverConsumer::ALL` is a **test-only constant**, and production code must not depend on it; **zero behavioral change** (only comments changed, and 4.4.2’s acceptance numbers remain unchanged; issue |                                                  | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method loses its formal-name table when called with named arguments (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closeout): a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) called with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, as do named-argument calls within a single file. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, and `main.yx` contains `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, while `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 classification: Class C** (old behavior was not successful: named arguments were silently dropped, followed by runtime failure or a silent wrong value). **Scope (final form after two rounds of narrowing on 2026-11-26—add only three items; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—obtain declared formal names from the unique cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` using the definition-unit qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` (candidate ↔ mixed IR name ↔ formal-name vectors are in the same order, matching the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table instead of using two separate bare names. These two locations fix only cross-unit methods with **bare-name imports** (`local == target`); candidate injection retains the pre-4.9.9 narrowing rule (skip when `local != target`), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**Class C (independent of the original bug): eliminate “multiple results for the same input” caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix of the original bug; criterion = the same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders, only one single binding allowed per method key; removing ascending-order merge produces two results). **Criteria (red before green)**: driver-level `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` has 2 cases (bare-import single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header records the medical-history gate); unit `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (empty-name-table guard for `method_param_info` ⇒ None, with a non-empty table returned unchanged as a positive control); unit `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the determinism criterion above). Project fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (an intermediate state contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 basic fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` did not enter the final history). The line-count change is the necessary result of fixtures entering and leaving the corpus (`corpus_probe` regenerates byte-for-byte consistently with the committed baseline), **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (each named explicitly; old behavior = silent ignore or silent discard; D60② should-report-but-does-not, Class A)**: closure value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container constructors other than `len` named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two items are corrected according to P0’s measured semantics**: ① **static-function forms** (both same-unit and cross-unit, definition and binding forms) are **entirely unavailable today**—same-unit `check` reports E3006, cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; positional and named arguments produce the same code, and this is unrelated to named arguments—it is not “named arguments are silently discarded”; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is not in the merged function table, again unrelated to named arguments. **Fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 Class A fixed in passing: old behavior E6007/E1014 was not successful, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arm** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). Two identity-surface residuals remain, one of which is closed: the unit’s own same-named type + alias import (two same-named definition-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the unit’s own declaration) **has been closed with the 4.9.10-S2a import-surface convergence** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever moved with the annotation family, `checker.rs` **must** add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged verbatim;
measurement showed that 5.3 did **not** move it, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was
already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines long—they
increase navigation cost, reduce cohesion, and provide zero decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are deferred until the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (first-principles rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62’s end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> one compile-time-item system. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual-argument
> view and implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a
> **pure decision** (identical after normalizing both sides; it does not bind type variables);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value
> environment/single-value pinning/Γ equations); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0
> (holding for closed terms and open terms/recursion alike); Σ construction points **reuse** the
> same evidence interface rather than establishing another one. **The completion criterion is that
> the invariants hold, not that substage names have been checked off.**

> **Partial order (not a serial chain)**: A facts → {A.C3, B.d, C.2, D design}; B kernel → {B.d,
> C.2, D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans toward typecheck→mono, and d toward types/solver→sema); C.2
> may run in parallel with B.d after 6.9.2-B/6.9.3a (it does not depend on defeq); D implementation
> waits for confirmation of the B design package; it depends on A (q=0 erasure) and C.1 (dispatch),
> and may depend on the 6.9.3 typed exit. **P7 gate = A/B/C exits; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 adjudication (A adjudicated on 2026-11-16; measured)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter the request” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have
> been deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request
> is created, and the representation layer can already hold `k-1` in `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)`.
> **The adjudication is changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a
> representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: do not
> specialize); D-b evaluation point (mono only; C-1: reconstruct from the second field / C-2:
> restore from IR, both break the single representation/evaluator; C-3 = A); **F4-T termination**
> (naive firing pushes the recursion chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a: fold the condition
> within the instance / T-b: bounded firing + fall back to the original at the boundary / T-c: a
> termination layer or a specification change). **Measure first, then adjudicate; before
> measurement, do not treat “A is implementable” as a conclusion.** **User (2026-11-16):
> D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task; do not claim the
> complete I4 body.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 states that “a
> decision point first follows the unified path; after unified failure, equality may be used, but
> the partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; when may defeq be attempted (only when both sides are ground, with no unbound
> variables); what are the snapshot/restoration boundaries and costs; and do unify and defeq share
> one budget or have separate budgets. **Responsibility boundary**: unify continues to handle
> subtyping/Any/Never; defeq only decides equivalence and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the connection contract in 6.9.3c has already
> wasted two rounds by assuming `can_assign` was the decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has
> zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if emission points/the code table changes);
> ④ behavioral changes classified according to D59 and made red before green. **Connection tasks
> additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many
> paths, which are reachable); using unit-test reachability to masquerade as user reachability is
> forbidden; rollback and budget require measured figures. **Residual disposition**: #537 (Class D,
> silent discard of proof-function formal refinement; not fixed before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5
> must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; C-stage boundary; if not closed, 6.9.4 only
> covers within a module), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 was closed on
> 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 +
> E0019, see the 3.20.30 row in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—on 2026-11-16, three locations moved
> in and out together: `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` /
> `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the single-point `rewritten_call_target`;
> the init section and function bodies share one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three
> mutations), #542 (orphaned shared layer; **implemented (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two
> entry-point connections + C2c temporary-avoidance removal; red→green, 402/402, function-table
> attribution and deviations), #552 (proof execution for imported multi-parameter predicates;
> adjacent to 6.9.5, separate case). **Ownership pending adjudication**: the four open-constraint
> tripwires (`Eq(N, n)`) in `rfc027_refined_transparency` do not belong to 6.9.4’s constant-equation
> bridge; decide whether they remain in 6.9.4’s outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/E4018’s proof-function
> surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness fields), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim the complete Π/Σ body; 6.9.4 only implements constant equations and
> does not fulfill the `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; `f(y)(y)`’s second value position is outside this item
> (E1002); witness erasure ≠ Runtime check erasure; if #537 is not fixed, 6.9.4/6.9.5 only cover
> forms that do not depend on proof-function formal refinement; if #539 is not fixed, 6.9.4 only
> covers within a module; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 is implemented (2026-11-19); 2.1.4’s
> inner-isolation red state was cleared on 2026-11-20 (the criterion was rewritten by slot identity
> in the 2.1.4 closeout) ⇒ all prerequisites for promoting `verify` to a gate are cleared.

**Hard acceptance** (**criteria revised on 2026-10-27, following the 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Directly driven test files** under `tests/` (tests that drive changed code, such as
`tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when required by mechanical changes, but each
**file / line count / reason** must be recorded; **tests must not be deleted and assertions must not
be relaxed**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch (new diagnostic code + baseline
update), does not fall under this hard acceptance requirement, and is a separate, separately
adjudicated round.

> **Revision relationship**: the original criteria (2026-10-26 decision ②) were written as
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, making the entire `tests/` directory a single zero-difference
> requirement; the revised criteria **change only directly driven test files from “zero difference”
> to “may be modified, but file / line count / reason must be recorded”**; the **zero-difference
> requirement for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and
> standard library (`src/std/`) remains unchanged**. First application = 6.1.2: only
> `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed, with **3 lines** (2 `assert_format_eq` changes from
> `i64` to `Int64` + 1 comment line), because the changed spelling requires the expected type name
> in that assertion to be updated in sync; no tests were deleted and no assertions were relaxed. See
> “P6 6.1 Name Normalization Closeout.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer **silently changes
associativity** (no error, only a different parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must enter both the
table and the cross-validation tests.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code refers back to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3’s prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) can proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criteria-infrastructure construction; but **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver
> requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x is precisely the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must **be written red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; the reverse order would cause bugs to be fixed into “established behavior” by the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g’s (#399) deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list appears in §P3.5 of this document)—the reverse order means redoing the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise, regressions cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | Type representations must converge first, or the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = exits A/B/C of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and 6.9.4 complete), and D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface and must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite for P7 and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and the 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count acquire their final forms only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                        | Members                                                                               | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                               | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                         |
| B                                            | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                         | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| C                                            | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                       | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| D                                            | 4.4 (proof-layer closeout) ∥ the entire P6 line                                       | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1-S4”                                                                                                                                                                          |
| E                                            | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                                 | All are mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| F                                            | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced under P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| G                                            | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                          | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` sites under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (B6/E5 are
in the same file batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track’s `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must run serially).

**New internal document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move batch prerequisite for P7), and 7b’s `Phi` arm
must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “post-hoc checks,” whereas rules
  are “prior judgment.” P9’s scripts cannot prevent “patching what should have been refactored”;
  only the D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists in original gap G3
  made closure impossible. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each owned by one phase
  (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hard-gate conversion
  points explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to do after the
  refactoring”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactoring means redoing the same deletions on the new
  grammar, new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341`
  into 7e and incorporating RFC status corrections into S4.
- **P5’s steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the granularity at which it can be
  rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero caller changes” as its hard acceptance criterion**—the split must be
  independently revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says “fixed defects must
  not be rolled back” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution convention**:
  the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must cite the fixed test name and defect description as a
  post-hoc bisect anchor.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into the two exclusive
  commits 7b.1a / 7b.1b under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references, and a missed rename
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 lands as 7e.1,
  and D20 lands as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation is merged into 7e.1, with the deletion
  action left to P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally to be “independent issues”**~~ **Fixed
  (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core language
  semantics and must not be left as an unimplemented remnant.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode-gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.

| C6          | The wasm playground fix requires P4’s `ProgramKind`                     | **The wasm-path vulnerability fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                        |
| C7          | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                      | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                                       |
| C8          | Correction of `upvalue_count` and the `.42` version number              | **Fix it + bump `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17                                                       |
